props.title: Switch back to Github Flow because of Lerna limitations
props.excerpt:
While trying to release v1.1.0, I faced some issues with Lerna.
The new ADR in this PR explains the rationale and the decision to switch back the Github Flow (thus amending https://github.com/thomvaill/log4brains/pull/121)

props.text: The team wants to record architectural decisions in the project.
props.quote: We want to record architectural decisions made in this project

props.text: The MADR format is lean and fits the team's development style.
props.quote: The MADR format is lean and fits our development style

props.text: The MADR structure is comprehensible and facilitates usage and maintenance.
props.quote: The MADR structure is comprehensible and facilitates usage & maintenance

props.text: The MADR project is vivid.
props.quote: The MADR project is vivid

props.text: The team wants the core library to be well-tested and developed with DDD and hexagonal architecture, which a monolith does not support.
props.quote: We don't want a monolith because we want the core library/API to be very well tested and probably developed with DDD and hexagonal architecture

props.text: The team is uncertain about future features, making the multi-package structure good for extensibility.
props.quote: As we are not so sure about the features we will provide in the future, this is good for extensibility

props.text: Yarn and Lerna are considered a good practice used by many open-source projects for publishing npm packages.
props.quote: Yarn + Lerna seems to be a very good practice used by a lot of other open-source projects to publish npm packages

props.text: Airbnb code style is widely used.
props.quote: Airbnb code style is widely used (see [npm trends](https://www.npmtrends.com/eslint-config-airbnb-vs-eslint-config-google-vs-standard-vs-eslint-config-standard))

props.text: Prettier-ESLint enforces additional code style, reducing debates.
props.quote: Prettier-ESLint enforce some additional code style. We like it because the more opinionated the code style is, the less debates there will be :-)

props.text: The system needs to uniquely identify ADRs for web URLs and CLI command arguments.
props.quote:
We need to be able to identify uniquely an ADR, especially in these contexts:

- Web: to build its URL
- CLI: to identify an ADR in a command argument (example: "edit", or "preview")

props.text: ADR titles can be duplicated, making them unsuitable as unique identifiers.
props.quote: It is possible to have duplicated titles

props.text: Other ADR tools already use the number as a unique ID.
props.quote: Other ADR tools like [adr-tools](https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools) already use the number as a unique ID

props.text: Using incremental numbers causes git merge conflicts when multiple developers create ADRs on separate branches.
props.quote: It causes an issue during a `git merge` when two developers have created a new ADR on their respective branch

props.text: The date-based filename format ensures files remain correctly sorted in the IDE.
props.quote: the files will still be correctly sorted in the IDE thanks to the date

props.text: Links between ADRs must be replaced with correct URLs
props.quote: Links between ADRs have to be replaced with correct URLs

props.text: The header must be rendered with specific components
props.quote: Header (status, date, deciders etc...) has to be rendered with specific components

props.text: The team may develop a VSCode extension in the future
props.quote: Potential future development of a VSCode extension

props.text: The project must provide a search bar for full-text search on ADRs
props.quote: We have to provide a search bar to perform full-text search on ADRs

props.text: The search solution must work in both preview mode and the statically built version
props.quote: Works in preview mode AND in the statically built version

props.text: The search solution must provide good fuzzy search and stemming capabilities
props.quote: Provides good fuzzy search and stemming capabilities

props.text: The search solution must be fast enough to show results while typing
props.quote: Is fast enough to be able to show results while typing

props.text: Log4brains is intended for all projects, not especially JS ones
props.quote: Since Log4brains is intended for all projects, not especially JS ones, we have to make the installation procedure simpler and language-agnostic

props.text: The current installation procedure does not work for non-JS projects
props.quote: For non-JS projects, you have to install manually the packages and the `npx init-log4brains` script does not work

props.text: The team prioritizes simplicity of the installation procedure
props.quote: Simplicity of the installation procedure

props.text: The existing GitHub Flow process lacked clarity for stable releases and was overly manual.
props.quote: The existing GitHub Flow process lacked clarity for stable releases and was overly manual, making it hard to delegate and streamline contributions

props.text: The project needs automation in releases.
props.quote: Need for automation in releases

props.text: The project needs to merge quickly without breaking the stable branch while allowing beta testers to test new features.
props.quote: Be able to merge more quickly whithout breaking the stable branch, while making it possible for beta testers to test the new features

props.text: The project requires easier delegation to new maintainers.
props.quote: Easier delegation to new maintainers

props.text: Lerna does not integrate well with Git Flow processes when managing both a develop and a stable branch.
props.quote: Specifically, **Lerna**, which we use for managing our monorepo, does not integrate well with Git Flow processes ([Lerna issue #2023](https://github.com/lerna/lerna/issues/2023#issuecomment-480402592)), when managing both a `develop` and `stable` branches: we cannot make Lerna publish a stable release from a different branch than the main one

props.text: The team needs automation in releases.
props.quote: Need for automation in releases

props.text: The team needs to merge quickly without breaking the stable branch while allowing beta testers to test new features.
props.quote: Be able to merge more quickly whithout breaking the stable branch, while making it possible for beta testers to test the new features

props.text: The team needs a simplified yet structured process for contributors.
props.quote: Simplified yet structured process for contributors
